answer.question: Which offices are under that cards per hour?
answer.answer:
Based on the documents, there is no specific view or metric that directly tracks which offices are under the cards per hour needed rate. The documents provide the definition and calculation method for cards per hour, but do not include a view that compares each office's current pace to the needed rate.

To determine which offices are under the needed cards per hour rate, we would need to:

1. Calculate the current cards per hour for each office using the last 7 days of data.
2. Compare this rate to the cards per hour needed rate, which is the remaining cards needed divided by the expected working hours before the deadline.

Since the program data does not provide this comparison directly, we cannot answer which offices are under the needed cards per hour rate without additional calculations.

I can't confirm that from the program data or documents. The necessary comparison is not provided in the available views or metrics.

An office is under the needed rate when its last 7 days rate is below the program-wide rate needed.

cases.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?

answer.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?
answer.answer:
Flash knocking is defined as recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. Specifically, a shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking results in the knocks in the flagged window being rolled back, meaning they are removed from the count of doors and contacts, even though they remain in the data with `rolled_back = true`.

- Threshold for flash knocking: 10 consecutive knocks in less than 30 seconds [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Confirmed flash knocking rolls back the flagged knocks [doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]
- Each open flag needs a conversation between the field lead and the canvasser before the next shift [doc:qc-rules#what-happens-after-a-flag]
- Contact rate is calculated as contacts (knocks with "canvassed" result) divided by doors [doc:counting-doors#contacts-and-contact-rate]

sources.text: Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts. A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full.

When QC confirms flash knocking, the knocks in the flagged window are rolled back: they stay in the data with rolled_back = true but are removed from doors and contacts. Rollbacks happen after the day's client report has been pulled, so they never change a report that was already sent.

Every open flag needs a conversation between the field lead and the canvasser before the canvasser's next shift, using the timestamped evidence on the flag. After the conversation the flag is marked reviewed. Two or more householding or flash knocking flags in one week for the same canvasser go to the field director.

A contact is a knock with the result "canvassed", meaning the canvasser spoke with the voter. Not home, refused and inaccessible are not contacts. Contact rate is contacts divided by doors for the same period and office.

cases.question: When does payroll run, and who has to approve overtime?

answer.question: When does payroll run, and who has to approve overtime?
answer.answer:
Payroll runs Tuesday at noon for the week that ended Sunday. Every shift must be approved by Monday at 5 PM; any shift not approved by then rolls to the next payroll. [doc:payroll-rules#payroll-deadline]

Overtime is approved by the field director for any shift that takes a person over 40 paid hours in a payroll week, Monday through Sunday. Hours over 40 are paid at 1.5 times the hourly rate. [doc:payroll-rules#overtime]

Canvassers are paid hourly by role: canvasser, field lead, registration canvasser and registration lead. Rates are in the pay rates table. Paid hours are clock in to clock out for each shift. [doc:payroll-rules#pay-rates]

A regular canvasser has worked 5 or more days in the program. A one-day hire worked exactly one day. An active canvasser worked at least one shift in the last 7 days. These definitions apply to GOTV canvassers. [doc:program-plan#staff-definitions]

A shift marked needs_fix cannot be paid until a field lead corrects it. Common reasons are a missing clock out (no paid hours yet) and a shift clocked under the wrong office. Fix the record, then mark it approved. [doc:payroll-rules#shifts-that-need-fixing]

Cards per hour is valid cards divided by paid registration hours. Current pace uses the last 7 days. The cards per hour needed from here is the cards still needed (goal minus valid cards) divided by the hours we expect to work before the deadline: average daily registration hours of the last 7 days times days left. An office is under the needed rate when its last 7 days rate is below the program-wide rate needed. [doc:registration-drive#cards-per-hour]

sources.text: Payroll for the week that ended Sunday runs Tuesday at noon. Every shift must be approved by Monday at 5 PM; pending and needs_fix shifts left after that roll to the next payroll.

The overtime threshold is 40 paid hours in a payroll week, Monday through Sunday, counting every shift the person worked. Hours over 40 are paid at 1.5 times the hourly rate. Any shift that takes a person over 40 hours needs the field director's approval and stays pending until it is approved.
Canvassers are paid hourly by role: canvasser, field lead, registration canvasser and registration lead. Rates are in the pay rates table. Paid hours are clock in to clock out for each shift.

A regular canvasser has worked 5 or more days in the program. A one-day hire worked exactly one day. An active canvasser worked at least one shift in the last 7 days. These definitions apply to GOTV canvassers.

A shift marked needs_fix cannot be paid until a field lead corrects it. Common reasons are a missing clock out (no paid hours yet) and a shift clocked under the wrong office. Fix the record, then mark it approved.

Cards per hour is valid cards divided by paid registration hours. Current pace uses the last 7 days. The cards per hour needed from here is the cards still needed (goal minus valid cards) divided by the hours we expect to work before the deadline: average daily registration hours of the last 7 days times days left. An office is under the needed rate when its last 7 days rate is below the program-wide rate needed.

cases.question: How should a canvasser record a locked apartment building?

answer.question: How should a canvasser record a locked apartment building?
answer.answer:
A canvasser should record a locked apartment building by marking it as "inaccessible" on its first unit and moving on, rather than marking each unit. This is because every apartment unit is its own door and must be knocked on individually. If a building is locked and the canvasser cannot get in, they should record the building once and continue canvassing other doors.

- Mark the building as "inaccessible" on its first unit [doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units].
- Do not mark each unit individually [doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units].
- Householding is not appropriate for a whole building from the lobby [doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units].

sources.text: Every apartment unit is its own door and must be knocked on its own. If a building is locked and the canvasser cannot get in, record the building once as "inaccessible" on its first unit and move on; do not mark each unit. A canvasser who marks a whole building from the lobby is householding.

sources.text: A contact is a knock with the result "canvassed", meaning the canvasser spoke with the voter. Not home, refused and inaccessible are not contacts. Contact rate is contacts divided by doors for the same period and office.

Pace compares doors to date with the goal to date. The projection for Election Day assumes nothing changes: doors to date plus the average daily doors of the last 7 days times the knocking days left. An office "will miss goal" when its projection is below its total goal; the shortfall is the goal minus the projection.

When projected capacity for the rest of the program (average daily doors of the last 7 days times days left) is larger than the untouched doors left in our turf, we will run out of first-pass turf. In that case ask the client for more doors first; new turf contacts voters at the normal first-pass rate. A second pass on not-home doors is the fallback, because second passes contact voters at roughly half the first-pass rate. If untouched doors exceed capacity, keep working the turf we have.

An attempt is every knock record the canvassing app submits. If a canvasser knocks a not-home door at 11:00 and comes back at 14:00, that is two attempts and one door. Attempts are always equal to or higher than doors.

sources.text: Riverbend Votes is a paid GOTV door canvass run from three offices: Northside, Eastgate and Harbor. Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts. A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full.
